units: sigma/m in cm^2/g; velocities in km/s

conventions.evaluation: Model value is <sigma_V v^n>/<v^n> over f(v) ~ v^2 exp(-v^2/(4 sigma_1D^2)), with sigma_1D = sqrt(pi)/4 times the mean relative velocity and n = moment, on a logarithmic grid of mean relative velocities across mean_relative_velocity_range_kms. The requirement has to hold over the whole range, so the smallest value is compared with minimum_cm2_g.
conventions.velocity: Ren et al. (arXiv:1808.05695) use <sigma v_rel> = sigma (4/sqrt(pi)) sigma_v0 with sigma_v0 the one-dimensional dark-matter velocity dispersion, i.e. n = 1 and <v> = 4 sigma_v0/sqrt(pi). Tulin & Yu (arXiv:1705.02358, Table I) quote v_rel without a precise definition; it is treated here as the mean relative velocity.
conventions.status: These are not exclusion limits. They are the cross sections for which self-interactions produce the cores inferred in dwarf and low-surface-brightness galaxies. The analyses assume that all of the dark matter is self-interacting and a constant sigma/m.

sets.default: Cores in dwarf and LSB spiral galaxies, sigma/m >~ 1 cm^2/g at v_rel = 30-200 km/s (Tulin & Yu, Table I).
sets.all: Every entry: also the SPARC rotation-curve sample mapped to relative velocities, and the too-big-to-fail values.

requirements.label: Cores in dwarf and LSB spiral galaxies (Tulin & Yu 2018, Table I)
requirements.notes: Table I row 'Cores in spiral galaxies (dwarf/LSB)': sigma/m >~ 1 cm^2/g at v_rel = 30-200 km/s from rotation curves. Text: 'Dwarf and LSB galaxies favor cross sections of at least 1 cm^2/g to produce large enough core radii'. Caption: the values 'assume constant sigma/m' and 'may be interpreted as a function of collisional velocity v_rel provided sigma/m is not steeply velocity-dependent'.

requirements.label: SPARC rotation curves (Ren et al. 2019; Kamada et al. 2017)
requirements.notes: Ren et al. fix sigma/m = 3 cm^2/g for 135 SPARC galaxies with V_f from 20 to 300 km/s and state that the results 'remain the same qualitatively for other values larger than ~1 cm^2/g on galaxy scales'; they do not fit a lower limit, and fits of high-surface-brightness galaxies are insensitive to sigma/m. Kamada et al. (arXiv:1611.02716) fix the same 3 cm^2/g for 30 galaxies with V_f in the 25-300 km/s range and note that sigma/m ~ 1 also gives good fits for V_f >~ 200 km/s. The velocity range is an assumption of this table: <v> = (4/sqrt(pi)) sigma_v0 = 1.44 V_f, using sigma_v0 = 0.64 V_max (Yang & Yu, arXiv:2205.03392) and V_max = V_f.

requirements.label: Too-big-to-fail, Milky Way (Tulin & Yu 2018, Table I)
requirements.notes: Table I: sigma/m >~ 0.6 cm^2/g at v_rel = 50 km/s from stellar dispersions.
